lesson.subtitle: Lesson 5 -- The Status Call
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Joyce Michalczuk | Lesson 5 -- The Status Call

listenings.text: I have run the global close calendar for eight years, and I have one rule for status calls. Do not bring me a problem without a plan. If you tell me the Brazil numbers are late, the next question is always the same: what are you doing about it, and when will I have them? So before you raise your hand, have that answer ready. We have already fixed the bank issue, we are still waiting for two invoices, and I will send the final file by Thursday at noon. That is a status. Anything else is just worry, and worry in a global call spreads very fast.

I disagree with the idea that you need a plan before you speak. I manage controllers in six countries, and the worst surprises I have had came from people who waited. They saw the problem on Monday, they wanted to solve it first, and I heard about it on Friday, when it was too late to help. So my rule is the opposite. Flag the risk the day you see it, even if you do not have the answer yet. Say what you know, what you do not know yet, and when you will know more. A risk I hear early is a risk I can manage. A risk I hear late is a crisis.
